title: sse: fix streaming chunking & event framing for partial JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Daniel Park
description:
Motivation: several customers and internal canaries observed invalid/malformed streaming events from the OpenAI-compat SSE layer when responses are emitted as fragmented token chunks. Symptoms included partial JSON objects arriving in a single SSE 'data:' event, missing event delimiters between logical messages, and rare token-ordering races when the chunker flushed mid-object. Root cause: the streaming chunker used tokenized emission boundaries without a robust framing layer that guarantees whole-event boundaries or sequence metadata; race between encoder flusher and SSE writer could reorder chunk flushes. Changes: 1) Introduced a dedicated framing layer that guarantees event delimiters ("data: ...

") and enforces whole-JSON-object emission when possible; 2) Buffering policy: small partial-object chunks are buffered until a syntactically-complete JSON object can be emitted or until a configurable timeout/size threshold is reached; 3) Added sequence_id and chunk_index internal headers on SSE events (internal only, visible in debug mode) to allow clients to detect reorder and reassemble if necessary; 4) Updated OpenAI-compat layer to strictly follow the "data: <json>

" model and to emit the terminal "data: [DONE]" event only after all buffered fragments have been flushed; 5) Added a compatibility shim for older clients that relied on per-token events: when compatibility mode is enabled we emit smaller chunks but guarantee a final object-complete event for each response part. Testing: unit tests for framing logic, integration tests simulating chunked TCP streams and delayed flusher, end-to-end test against SSE curl clients and node-fetch SSE harness. Rollout: gated behind feature flag sse_chunker_v2, enabled for canary hosts for 48h then rolled to main. Checklist: [x] unit tests updated/added, [x] integration tests added, [x] manual verification with curl/node SSE clients, [x] updated compatibility notes in docs, [x] canary rollout plan executed. Related: links to Linear ENG-2187 and incident SUP-4321 for customer reports.
